You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point.
- Each token in the group account pays 0.75 points to every member of the group, you included, whoever put it there.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking: This is a public goods game where each token contributed to the group returns 0.75 to each of 4 members, meaning 3 total but only 0.75 back to the contributor versus keeping the full point privately. So the dominant selfish strategy is to contribute nothing, though full cooperation maximizes group payoff, and I'm weighing whether to contribute something anyway to encourage mutual cooperation.

reply.thinking:
Each token I contribute returns only 0.75 to me but costs 1, so individually defecting is the dominant strategy. Yet if everyone contributes fully, we'd all net 60 per round instead of the 20 we'd get keeping everything—cooperation pays off collectively even though it's individually irrational.

I'll start with a moderate contribution of 10 tokens to signal willingness to cooperate without fully exposing myself to free-riders.
